findings.description: Between ~00:00.9 and 00:01.0 a second cube materializes directly beside the cube the hand is twisting. The hand never leaves the cube it is holding nor brings a new cube in from off-frame; the new cube simply splits out of the manipulated one.

While the hand only fingers the green cube at 00:02.75-00:03.00, a new cube emerges to its right (visible 00:03.0-00:03.25) with no carrying or placing motion. The same pattern recurs at ~00:04.0, ~00:05.0 and ~00:06.0: each twist of the end cube spawns an additional cube rather than a cube being brought in.

Dense frames 00:06.30-00:06.75 show the hand gripping a single green '3' cube; within ~1/12 s it becomes a green '2' cube plus a separate blue '3' cube next to it. A twisting action cannot produce a second object; the effect does not match the cause.
